chapter: Image, travel and Black, Brown and Beige
title: His parents never heard him play live
summary: Greer repeats that his family heard him only on radio and records, and his mother was proud.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But as I say, we played everywhere. I never played in my hometown, Long Branch, New Jersey. My mother and father never heard me play. My two sisters never heard me play. My little brother heard me once. That's one thing I always felt sorry for, my parents never lived to hear me playing, my sisters never heard me. We played everywhere but they never hired great big bands down there, you know, I mean an outfit was so expensive. But they heard about us because my mother and father kept up with our progress, you know.
Oh, yeah, they got records, didn't they? They just never heard you play live, personally.
Heard you play on the radio?

Yeah. But in person, no. But she knew I was climbing, she knew I was climbing. And she used to read about the different progress of our band, you know. Man, she was so proud. The whole town was proud because I was the only one, white or colored, made the grade, from Long Branch. And anybody told my mother I would have went that far, never. Beyond expectations, you know.
